audit.whatIsWrong: Rated 8.5/10 'Hard matchup' with an 8.5/10 carry threat while Illaoi wins 58.53% over 2040 games — the page's own late text calls it 'one of Illaoi's best winrates on the board'.
audit.why: This is a large sample and the prose, the packet chart and the win rate all agree the lane is strongly Illaoi's after level 2. Only the difficulty tokens disagree.
audit.corrected: Chart fixed to the packet. diff/diffRating/carryRating left untouched — changing a 'hard' label to 'favoured' is a judgement about the whole page's scale, not a matchup fact. See questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Renekton levels 3, 6 and the 2-item stage and called 4-5 and first item Skill. The packet gives Renekton only levels 1-2 and Illaoi everything from level 3 on.
audit.why: whys[2] says level 3 flips it, whys[4] says 6 is 'firmly on your side', whys[6] says your tentacle DPS dominates the 2-item stage. Five of seven rows contradicted their own explanations, the packet, and a 58.53% win rate.
audit.corrected: phases[2,3,4,5,6].side and win[2,3,4,5,6] all set to Illaoi as matched pairs, with their ratings raised to 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ruthless Predator was tracked all over the page with no cooldown, no mention that the empowered version destroys damage shields, and no mention that it opens with an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Riot's text: W is 16/14/12/10/8s, stuns 0.75s normally and 1.5s above 50 Fury, and the empowered version destroys damage shields on the target. The _missing feed flags the auto-reset tell — the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue to step out. Cull the Meek heals him off every unit it hits, which is why Grievous Wounds decides extended trades (second _missing rule).
audit.corrected: 16s rank-1 cooldown and the auto-reset tell written into spikes[0].text; the Q heal and Executioner's Calling written into spikes[2].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on the tracked ability.
audit.why: W at 16s rank 1 and Slice and Dice at 16s rank 1 are both long; baiting either opens a full Illaoi pattern.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] said Renekton can 'cleanse' Test of Spirit.
audit.why: Cleanse and QSS eligibility is explicitly not in the kit data, and the brief says empty means unknown, never 'yes'. Telling a player his soul can be cleansed changes when they spend a 16s ability.
audit.corrected: Rewrote it to dodging only, with the cooldown cost of a whiff.

edits.before: Your Level 3 is where the matchup flips: with W Harsh Lesson up you outsustain his empowered combo, and if he dashes in you can slam a Tentacle onto him and drop E Test of Spirit for a real threat.
edits.after: Level 3 flips it: Ruthless Predator (W) is 16s at rank 1 and its wind-up is an auto reset — step back on the wind-up, not the cast. When he Slice and Dices in, Tentacle him and drop Test of Spirit.

edits.before: After your first item (usually Iceborn or Trailblazer into bruiser) your Tentacle slams outdamage his fury windows, and any all-in he throws feeds your passive stacks.
edits.after: After your first item your Tentacle slams out-damage his fury windows, but Cull the Meek heals him off every minion — Executioner's Calling turns his trade into a losing one.

edits.before: Dodge or cleanse your E so his soul is never taken
edits.after: Dodge your E so his soul is never taken — 16s wasted

notes: Chart was wrong on five of seven rows against both the packet and a 58.53% win rate over 2040 games. The empowered W destroying damage shields is worth knowing if the player runs Sterak's — I did not write it into a length-capped field, but it belongs in the ability breakdown if a slot opens. Removed the claim that Renekton can cleanse Test of Spirit: cleanse eligibility is not in the data. The packet defect 'never names any of Renekton's abilities' is only half true — the content layer uses lowercase 'ruthless-predator' and 'Slice-and-Dice' rather than proper names, which is probably what the checker missed.
